content: Litharge is one of the naturally occurring mineral forms of lead(II) oxide, chemically represented as PbO. It is classified as a secondary mineral, which forms as a result of the oxidation of galena ores. Litharge typically appears as coatings or encrustations and exhibits an internal tetragonal crystal structure. It is dimorphous with massicot, which is the orthorhombic form of lead(II) oxide. The mineral litharge was first officially described in 1917, based on its occurrence in San Bernardino County, California. Historically, the term litharge has been used to describe other similar substances. For instance, litharge of gold refers to litharge mixed with red lead, which gives it a reddish hue. Litharge of silver is a by-product obtained during the process of separating silver from lead. Similarly, litharge of bismuth is a product resulting from the oxidation of bismuth. Additionally, the term litharge has been used interchangeably with white lead or red lead in certain contexts.
